reply_text:
I found one new candidate for 2025 and met the claim you already have. The new one is weak: a short time span from Sutskever's June 6 University of Toronto speech.

**The recorded claim (2025-11-25, Dwarkesh Podcast).** Asked when a system that "can learn as well as a human" and then becomes superhuman would arrive, Sutskever said "I think like 5 to 20", and answered "Mhm" when asked "5 to 20 years?" I couldn't read this on Dwarkesh's own transcript page: it stopped at about minute 25 both times I opened it. The timestamped exchange (01:22:14–01:22:29) appears in a third-party Substack essay. Its earlier excerpts match the official page word for word, but you may want to check this one against the video.

**The new candidate (Toronto speech).** He said things will feel "much more real" in one to three years as AI improves. This is a forecast about intuition and perception, not a capability, so it is a borderline fit. The source is a third-party word-for-word transcript of the official YouTube video, without punctuation.

**A misreading to watch for.** The Decoder, Hans India and Daily8 all report that he predicted superintelligence in "three, five, maybe ten years". In the transcript he gives those numbers as other people's guesses ("some people say it's in three some people say it's in five 10 numbers are being thrown around") and then says "it's a bit hard to predict the future". His own line in that passage, "the day will come…", has no date, so I put it under undated.

**Two things that don't qualify.** In a November 28 post on X, he said scaling "won't stall" but "something important will continue to be missing". This has no date and isn't about when AGI arrives. I saw it only quoted in that Substack essay and didn't open the post itself. In the Dwarkesh interview he also called 2020–2025 "the age of scaling", which describes the past rather than predicting anything.

I used 8 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings. Two openings went to Dwarkesh's transcript page, because the first time the text came back in a form my script couldn't read.
